event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: WDC’s 2022 Form 10-K contains an extensive, multi-layered discussion of COVID-19 and broader pandemic-related risk.  The company confirms that the virus has already caused concrete, material impacts—ranging from temporary plant shutdowns to $248 million of incremental logistics and factory charges—and warns that similar or larger effects may persist.  The disclosure spans direct operational hits (labour safety measures, under-absorbed overhead, component shortages), knock-on financial pressures (credit-market deterioration, higher borrowing costs, margin compression) and systemic vulnerabilities (remote-work cyber-risk, supply-chain fragility).  While certain passages strike a cautious tone by stressing uncertainty or highlighting mitigation (e.g., sanitation protocols, facilities currently open), the bulk of language is specific, recent and linked to measured dollar figures, signalling a live, high-severity risk well within the 0-3-year window of the Time Decay Principle.  Taken together, the document portrays COVID-19 as an ongoing, enterprise-wide threat with both realised and potential future costs, warranting overall elevated risk scores despite partial offsets from mitigation efforts.
